supplied: body vtable slot 1 (query with 0x8002), hooked at an authored stub
method: The native routine runs unmodified in Unicorn with the two obfuscated stubs and the pool take hooked (stubs return as ret 8, which the native epilogue requires). Python external_pose_contacts runs on a copy with the same scripted services. The query service randomly rewrites body source dwords mid-routine so copy order is observable.
comparisons: ordered service calls with arguments (guard objects, pool object, body, mask)
all fixture bytes: link, both bodies, the reused record, the pool record, lock and pool objects
coverage: each body query true and false, with garbage in the upper 56 bits of rax
source bytes changed between the first and second body copies
limits: The obfuscated stubs are not run; their lock semantics are inferred from placement around the pool take.
The pool record is a synthetic 0xD0-byte buffer; its real size is not recovered.
The body virtual query is an authored stand-in; its meaning of mask 0x8002 is not recovered.
The owner argument is never read by the native routine and is not compared.
